findings.location: Proof 1.1, at the sentence beginning ‘Put Z and Q in general position relative to their boundary collars.’
findings.evidence: The statement allows finite rational 2-chains, but the cited def-oriented-intersection-number defines intersection for smooth maps from compact oriented smooth manifolds and for smooth submanifolds; it does not define an intersection product for the stated finite rational chains. Proof 1.1 obtains a finite rational singular 3-chain Z with boundary P-P', then asserts without a chain model or a cited relative chain-general-position result that Z and Q can be put in general position and that Z∩Q is a compact oriented 1-chain. The statement only assumes general position for P and Q, not this new Z. Supply/prove a relative smoothing and chain-intersection theorem preserving the collars, or restrict the chain inputs and prove the required independence in that category. This supplier is used by lem-slice-disk-induces-seifert-metabolizer in the locally flat isotropy argument.
